tools.description: Create a session from a tmuxp-style YAML workspace document: windows, panes, layouts, and the command each pane runs, in one call.
tools.name: build_workspace

tools.description: Run several tools in one request, in order, including the ones that end something. Stops at the first failure, and nothing it already ended comes back; the reply names the calls it skipped.

calls.description: the calls to run, in order

tool.description: the name of the tool to call

onError.description: what a failing call does to the calls after it; empty stops the batch

tools.name: call_destructive_tools_batch

tools.description: Run several tools in one request, in order, including ones that change tmux. Laying out a window is a split, a resize, and a command per pane; this makes it one call. Stops at the first failure, and what already ran stays, because tmux has no transaction; the reply names the calls it skipped.

calls.description: the calls to run, in order

tool.description: the name of the tool to call

onError.description: what a failing call does to the calls after it; empty stops the batch

tools.name: call_mutating_tools_batch

tools.description: Run several reading tools in one request, in order. Refuses the whole batch if any call would change tmux, so a batch believed to be read-only never alters a session. Stops at the first failure, and names the calls it skipped.

calls.description: the calls to run, in order

tool.description: the name of the tool to call

onError.description: what a failing call does to the calls after it; empty stops the batch

tools.name: call_readonly_tools_batch

tools.description: Read what one pane holds: its visible screen, or its scrollback too with includeHistory. The reply is bounded and says what it dropped. Pass styles for a program that reports success or failure in colour rather than in words, which a capture otherwise strips. Use capture_since instead to read a pane repeatedly without paying for the same screen each time.

endLine.description: last row to read, on the same scale as startLine

includeHistory.description: read scrollback as well as the visible screen

joinWrapped.description: rejoin lines the terminal wrapped, as tmux does it; a multi-row shell prompt can be joined to the line after it, so prefer run_command for output you ran yourself

maxBytes.description: how many bytes to return at most, keeping the last lines

maxLines.description: how many lines to return at most, keeping the last ones

paneId.description: a tmux pane id such as %1; empty reads the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to read when paneId is empty

startLine.description: first row to read; 0 is the top of the screen and negatives are history

styles.description: keep colour and attribute escape sequences, for a program that says pass or fail in colour rather than in words

tools.name: capture_pane

annotations.title: Read What a Pane Wrote Since

tools.description: Read only what a pane wrote since the cursor a previous call returned, and get a cursor for next time. Call it once with no cursor to start. This is how to watch a pane across turns: a quiet pane returns nothing rather than its whole screen again. linesMissed reports that tmux discarded scrollback in between, so the reply is the current screen rather than everything since.

cursor.description: the cursor a previous capture_since returned; empty starts a new reading

maxBytes.description: how many bytes to return at most, keeping the last lines

maxLines.description: how many lines to return at most, keeping the last ones

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to read; the cursor already names it

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to read when paneId is empty

tools.name: capture_since

tools.description: Clear a pane's screen, and its scrollback when asked. Clearing what has already been read keeps later captures small.

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to clear; empty clears the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to clear when paneId is empty

tools.name: clear_pane

tools.description: Start one session and return its id and name. The MCP runtime stays attached through its private control connection.

command.description: a command for the first window to run instead of a shell

tools.name: create_session

tools.description: Add one window to a session and return its id and the id of the pane tmux made with it. Use build_workspace instead when a whole session is being laid out from a document.

command.description: a command for the window to run instead of a shell

sessionName.description: the exact session name to add the window to

tools.name: create_window

tools.description: Remove a buffer in the libtmux-mcp- namespace once nothing else will paste it. A buffer left behind stays on the tmux server for anyone attached to paste by hand, and tmux keeps a bounded stack of them, so the oldest is dropped to make room for a new one.

name.description: the buffer to remove, as load_buffer returned it

tools.name: delete_buffer

tools.description: Expand a tmux format; tmux's #() syntax runs a shell command, so treat the format as operator-powerful. Use formats such as #{pane_current_path} or #{window_flags} to inspect anything about tmux that no tool here has its own answer for.

format.description: a tmux format string, such as #{pane_current_path}

paneId.description: the pane the format is about; empty uses the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to evaluate against when paneId is empty

tools.name: display_message

tools.description: Put a pane into tmux's copy mode, where keys scroll and select rather than reaching the program in the pane. Leave it with exit_copy_mode: keys sent to a pane still in copy mode do not reach the shell.

paneId.description: the tmux pane id; empty uses the active pane

scrollUp.description: enter one page above the bottom

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to use when paneId is empty

tools.name: enter_copy_mode

tools.description: Return a pane from copy mode to passing keys to the program running in it.

paneId.description: the tmux pane id; empty uses the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to use when paneId is empty

tools.name: exit_copy_mode

tools.description: Report the pane bordering one side of another: above, below, left, or right. Reads tmux's coordinates, so asking does not change which pane is active.

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to look from; empty looks from the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to look from when paneId is empty

tools.name: find_pane_by_position

tools.description: Collect a command started with run_command and detach. Without timeoutSeconds it reports whether the command has finished and returns at once, which is what to call between other work; with one it waits that long. A finished job reports its exit status and its output, and answers the same way however often you ask.

jobId.description: the handle a detached run_command returned

maxBytes.description: how many bytes to return at most, keeping the last lines

maxLines.description: how many lines of output to return at most, keeping the last ones

timeoutSeconds.description: wait up to this long for the command to finish; zero reports whether it has and returns at once

tools.name: get_job

tools.description: One pane's state without its contents: what it runs, its process id, whether that process has exited and with what status, how much scrollback there is, and whether the pane is in a mode that will eat the keys you send it.

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to describe; empty describes the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to describe when paneId is empty

tools.name: get_pane_info

tools.description: How to do one of the jobs this server is for, in the order that avoids the traps its tools have: diagnose_pane (what a pane is doing and why it is stuck), watch_pane (follow one across turns without re-reading it), recover_pane (get back one that stopped answering), set_up_workspace (lay out a session for a piece of work). The same text this server offers as MCP prompts.

argument.description: the pane id the recipe is about, such as %1, or for set_up_workspace what the workspace is for

tools.name: get_recipe

tools.description: Which tmux socket these tools address, its version, how much it holds, and whether this MCP server is itself running in one of its panes. Ask this first: insideThisServer true means a pane you act on may be the terminal this is running in.

includeMessages.description: add tmux's own server message log, which records what tmux refused and why

maxBytes.description: how many bytes of log messages to return at most, keeping the most recent

maxLines.description: how many log messages to return at most, keeping the most recent

tools.name: get_server_info

tools.description: One session's windows, working directory, and when it was created.

sessionName.description: the exact session name; empty uses the only session

tools.name: get_session_info

tools.description: One window's size, layout string, and panes. The layout string is what select_layout accepts back, so a layout worth keeping can be read here and applied later.

sessionName.description: which session's current window to describe when windowId is empty

windowId.description: the tmux window id to describe; empty describes the current window

tools.name: get_window_info

tools.description: End one pane and the program running in it. A pane that was its window's last takes the window with it, which the reply says.

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to kill, such as %1

tools.name: kill_pane

tools.description: End the whole tmux server: every session, every window, every program. Requires confirm to be true.

confirm.description: must be true; this ends every session on the server

tools.name: kill_server

tools.description: End one session by its exact name, and every window and program in it. Nothing brings it back.

sessionName.description: the exact name of the session to kill

tools.name: kill_session

tools.description: End one window and its panes. A window that was its session's last takes the session with it, which the reply says.

windowId.description: the tmux window id to kill, such as @1

tools.name: kill_window

tools.description: List tmux panes with their session, window, index, and current command. Narrow with sessionName, windowId, command, pathUnder, dead, or active rather than listing the server and discarding most of the answer: on a busy server that is the difference between one pane and forty. Ask for detail full to add each pane's exit status, path, title, and history size, which is how to check on several panes without capturing any of them. Returns an empty list when the server is not running.

active.description: keep only active panes, or only inactive ones

command.description: keep panes whose current command contains this text, ignoring case

dead.description: keep only panes whose process has exited, or only those still running

detail.description: how much to report per pane; full adds exit status, path, title, and history size

pathUnder.description: keep panes whose working directory is at or below this path

sessionName.description: list only this session's panes

windowId.description: list only this window's panes, such as @1

tools.name: list_panes

tools.description: The tmux servers running on this machine, with the one these tools address marked. tmux leaves a socket file behind when a server exits, so the ones nothing is listening on are left out unless includeDead asks for them. Discovery only: no tool here can be pointed at another one, which is decided when this server is started.

includeDead.description: include socket files with no server running, which tmux leaves behind when a server exits

maxServers.description: how many servers to report at most (default 100, maximum 1000); the target is always kept

name.description: keep servers whose name contains this text, ignoring case

tools.name: list_servers

tools.description: Sessions with their name, window count, and how many clients are attached. Narrow with name, or with attached to find which sessions somebody is actually looking at.

attached.description: keep only sessions a client is attached to, or only those nobody is watching

name.description: keep sessions whose name contains this text, ignoring case

tools.name: list_sessions

tools.description: Windows with their session, name, index, pane count, and whether each is its session's current one. Narrow with sessionName, name, or active.

active.description: keep only current windows, or only the others

name.description: keep windows whose name contains this text, ignoring case

sessionName.description: list only this session's windows

tools.name: list_windows

name.description: a name for the buffer; empty makes one up

text.description: the text to store in the buffer

tools.name: load_buffer

windowId.description: the tmux window id to move

delete.description: remove the buffer once it has been pasted

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to pipe when paneId is empty

sessionName.description: the exact session to rename; empty uses the only session

tools.name: rename_session

tools.description: Name a window, which also stops tmux renaming it after whatever is running in it.

sessionName.description: which session's current window to rename when windowId is empty

windowId.description: the tmux window id to rename; empty uses the current window

tools.name: rename_window

tools.description: Set one pane's width or height in cells, or toggle it between its layout size and the whole window. Reports the size tmux settled on, which a layout may constrain.

height.description: the pane's new height in cells

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to resize; empty resizes the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to resize when paneId is empty

width.description: the pane's new width in cells

zoom.description: toggle the pane between its size and the whole window

tools.name: resize_pane

tools.description: Set a window's size in cells. Worth doing before running something whose output is laid out in columns, since a window no client is attached to is whatever size tmux guessed.

height.description: the window's new height in cells

sessionName.description: which session's current window to resize when windowId is empty

width.description: the window's new width in cells

windowId.description: the tmux window id to resize; empty uses the current window

tools.name: resize_window

tools.description: Restart what a pane runs, keeping the pane and its place in the layout. Use it on a pane whose program exited rather than killing the pane and splitting a new one. A command that exits takes the pane with it, and the window if it was the last one: set remain-on-exit on the window first to keep it as a dead pane list_panes can report.

command.description: a command to run instead; empty restarts what the pane ran before

kill.description: end a program that is still running first

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to restart; empty uses the active pane

annotations.title: Run a Command in a Pane

tools.description: Run a POSIX-compatible shell command in one pane, wait for it to finish, and return its exit status and its output. Prefer this to send_keys followed by capture_pane: it does not read the screen to decide the command is done, so the shell's echo of the command cannot be mistaken for the command's output, and an exit status is something no capture recovers. Pass detach for a command you do not need the answer to yet, such as a build: it returns a jobId at once, you do other work, and get_job collects the status and the output later.

command.description: the POSIX-compatible shell command to run

detach.description: return a jobId at once instead of waiting; collect it later with get_job

maxBytes.description: how many bytes of output to return at most, keeping the last lines

maxLines.description: how many lines of output to return at most, keeping the last ones

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to run the command in; empty uses the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to run in when paneId is empty

suppressHistory.description: keep the command out of the shell's history by prefixing a space

timeoutSeconds.description: how long to wait before giving up

tools.name: run_command

tools.description: Find which panes show some text, and what they showed. Answers "which pane has the failing test" in one call, where capturing each pane in turn costs one per pane.

includeHistory.description: search scrollback as well as the visible screens

maxMatchesPerPane.description: how many matching lines to report per pane

maxPanes.description: how many matching panes to report at most

regex.description: read text as a regular expression

sessionName.description: search only this session's panes

text.description: text to look for in each pane's contents

tools.name: search_panes

layout.description: even-horizontal, even-vertical, main-horizontal, main-vertical, tiled, main-horizontal-mirrored or main-vertical-mirrored from tmux 3.5, or a layout string from get_window_info

sessionName.description: which session's current window to arrange when windowId is empty

spread.description: give every pane an equal share of the space

windowId.description: the tmux window id to arrange; empty uses the current window

tools.name: select_pane

tools.description: Make one window its session's current window, which is what puts a person in front of a window this client created.

windowId.description: the tmux window id to make current

literal.description: send the keys as characters rather than as tmux key names

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to send to; empty uses the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to send to when paneId is empty

tools.name: send_keys_batch

unset.description: remove the variable instead of setting it

tools.name: set_environment

name.description: the tmux option name, such as history-limit

paneId.description: the pane to set the option on

scope.description: the scope to set at; empty sets at pane scope

sessionName.description: the session to set the option on

windowId.description: the window to set the option on

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to title when paneId is empty

maxBytes.description: how many bytes to return at most, keeping the last lines

maxLines.description: how many lines to return at most, keeping the last ones

name.description: the buffer to read, as load_buffer returned it

tools.name: show_buffer

maxBytes.description: how many bytes of listing to return at most

maxLines.description: how many variables to return at most

name.description: the tmux option name, such as history-limit

paneId.description: the pane to read the option on

scope.description: the scope to read at; empty reads at pane scope

sessionName.description: the session to read the option on

windowId.description: the window to read the option on

tools.description: One pane's contents together with what it is, where it sits, and whether its process has exited. Prefer this to capture_pane followed by get_pane_info when one response is enough. State and content are collected sequentially, not atomically.

includeHistory.description: read scrollback as well as the visible screen

maxBytes.description: how many bytes to return at most, keeping the last lines

maxLines.description: how many lines to return at most, keeping the last ones

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to describe; empty describes the active pane

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to describe when paneId is empty

percentage.description: the new pane's share of the space, 1 to 100

tools.description: Wait until something signals a tmux wait-for channel. Timeout or cancellation ends this call but cannot remove tmux's global waiter; a later signal may be consumed by it, so do not reuse channel names.

tools.description: Wait until a pane writes one of several patterns. It takes one exact screen baseline after attaching, then reads what the pane produces without polling. Use it for output the client did not author, such as a service announcing it is ready. Pass stop with the markers of failure you already know, so a run that failed returns at once instead of at the deadline. Omit patterns to wait for any output at all. Matching retains the most recent one megabyte and reports any older prefix as truncation. When you cannot predict what finishing prints, set idleSeconds and wait for the pane to go quiet instead.

idleSeconds.description: end the wait once the pane has written nothing for this many seconds

maxBytes.description: how many bytes of output to return at most, keeping the last lines

maxLines.description: how many lines of output to return at most, keeping the last ones

paneId.description: the tmux pane id to watch; empty watches the active pane

patterns.description: any one of these ends the wait; empty waits for any output

regex.description: read the patterns as regular expressions

sessionName.description: which session's active pane to watch when paneId is empty

sinceEntry.description: ignore what the pane already shows and match only new output

stop.description: markers of failure that end the wait early, such as "error:"

timeoutSeconds.description: how long to wait before giving up
